issues.detail: The Hebrew 'אֵילִם' means 'rams' (male sheep), but the Chinese renders it as '公綿羊' (male sheep) while rendering 'עַתֻּדִים' (he-goats) as '公羊' (male goat/sheep). The order and species are swapped: Hebrew lists rams (אֵילִם) then he-goats (עַתֻּדִים), but Chinese lists '公羊' (he-goats) first then '公綿羊' (rams), reversing the two categories.
